question: Who writes a brigade's builder (CSubUnit +0x34), which saves name the owner on nearly every brigade

addresses.name: CDistributeUpgrade::Distribute
addresses.signature: CFixedPoint* __thiscall CDistributeUpgrade::Distribute(CDistributeUpgrade* this, CFixedPoint* out@stack:4, __int64 available@stack:8, bool flag@stack:16)
addresses.comment:
**Slot 0, read through**: 0x51CE60 to the `ret 0x10` at 0x51D5B5. budget = base_percentage x available x factor in thousandths; free = the same share of lend_lease_ic. It zeroes its own +0x20 (an __int64, the count of brigades upgrading in fixed 15, which the tooltip prints as UNITS) and CCountry +0xAA4, upgrade_cost. The list is the country's second unit list (+0xBBC, the units it lent out) **first** and then its own units (+0xBAC) less those with an expeditionary owner, each needing upgrade_active (+0xA5), a unit with +0xA4 set going to the front.

For every node of every brigade's `technologies` whose technology has canUpgrade (+0x314) and whose level is below the country's level_by_technology (or, for a government in exile, the first member of its faction's if higher): days = CCountry::GetBuildTime(country, the brigade's definition, 0); rate = max(1000000 / (days x 1000) x 2, g_UpgradeLeastRate) x the SHIP_/AIR_/LAND_UPGRADE_SPEED_MOD define, **thousandths of a level a day**. cost = BuildCostIC x (1000 + build_cost_by_unit_type - GetCategoryBuildDiscount) / 1000, x (1000 + RESERVES_PENALTY_SIZE) / 1000 for a reserve; daily = cost / the brigade's technology count x g_ReinforcementDailyShare / levels behind. **A technology whose `change` (+0x288) is clear - a doctrine - costs nothing and moves a whole level a day.** Where daily is more than the budget left, the progress is budget x 2 x rate / 1000 and the rest of the budget is paid; after that nothing more moves. progress is added to the node's +0x8; at 1000 it goes back to zero and the level goes up one, and **where the technology's `change` is set, the brigade's builder (CSubUnit +0x34/+0x38) becomes its owner (+0x94/+0x98)** - unless the unit's expeditionary_owner id (CUnit +0x290) is this country's id (+0xCA8), a unit the country lent out and is upgrading through +0xBBC (0x51D48F..0x51D4CD); a doctrine names nobody; and after the brigade's last technology CUnit::RebuildDefinition is called on its unit. upgrade_cost takes every `daily`, spent or not - the slider's need. Resources are charged once at the end for what was spent less `free`. It ignores the flag and returns zero.

**Checked against a savegame two days in**: with the save's shares and the laws the day ran under, two days of this reproduce the `{level progress}` pair on all 1,469 of Germany's technology lines, including the wing the share ran out on (0.008 where its neighbours have 0.020) and the three after it with nothing. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitdaily.md, section 5.
addresses.revises: adds the write of a brigade's builder at a whole level (0x51D48F..0x51D4CD), which the record had as 'another writer, not found', and marks the lent units' list as walked first
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x51D475..0x51D4CD: `add [eax+8], esi; cmp [eax+8], 0x3E8; jl` - `mov [eax+8], 0; inc [eax+4]` (the level-up), then `mov eax,[esp+0x38]; cmp byte [eax+0x288], 0; je skip` (the technology's change), `mov edx,[esp+0x58]; mov edx,[edx+0x290]; cmp edx,[country+0xCA8]; je skip` ([esp+0x58] is the unit, loaded from the list node at 0x51D1E0), then `mov edx,[brigade+0x94]; mov [brigade+0x34],edx; mov edx,[brigade+0x98]; mov [brigade+0x38],edx`. List build: +0xBBC walked at 0x51CF6D before +0xBAC at 0x51D04A, both appending (priority prepending). Saves: every brigade that gained `builder` between two saves of one game had a level of a technology with change rise (1,253 of 1,253 from Germany1936_01_01_00 to Germany1936_04_20_03 bar 6 annexed from Guangxi, 390 of 390 Ireland1936_02_06_02 to _03_11_04), and every brigade whose equipment level rose without gaining it stood in a unit with expeditionary_owner (17 of 17 non-mismatched, Ireland1940_05_23_20 to 1941_07_16_07). What would show it wrong: a brigade gaining builder with no level of a changing technology risen, in a unit not lent - none found.

struct_fields.name: builder
struct_fields.comment: Who built it, saved as `builder` where the id half of the tag is set, read back by CSubUnit::LoadKey; the constructor writes `---`. **Two writers**: CMilitaryConstruction::Deliver sets it from the line's builder (+0x50/+0x54) only where that is not the line's country (0x484E7E..0x484E8F) - a licence's seller; and CDistributeUpgrade::Distribute sets it to the brigade's owner (+0x94/+0x98) at every whole level of a technology whose `change` is set, unless the unit is one the paying country lent out (0x51D48F..0x51D4CD). So a brigade of the country's own line has none until its first whole level of equipment, and a save's `builder` names the owner on nearly every brigade (3,519 of the 3,732 that carry one in Ireland1941_07_16_07; the rest licence-built and not upgraded since, or changed hands after their last upgrade - CUnit_SetOwner rewrites +0x94, never this). The summary, the brigade card and a sunk ship's row name a brigade's model from this country's set where it is set, else the owner's.
struct_fields.revises: the second writer found: the upgrade share (was 'another writer sets it - not found')
struct_fields.evidence: Store scan over .text for a dword store to [r+0x34] followed within eight instructions by one to [r+0x38] through the same register: 669 hits, 418 not through esp/ebp; the two whose value comes from a country tag or a line's builder are 0x51D4C4 (Distribute, from +0x94/+0x98) and 0x484E8C (Deliver, from the line's +0x50/+0x54 - the positive control). The five qword stores to [r+0x34] are in unrelated functions (StratWarfare_SetChartSeries, CBrigadePicker's constructor, map code). A writer copying the tag by memcpy or a whole-object copy would not show; the saves are the check on that: no brigade gained builder without a level of a changing technology rising, in six stretches.

struct_fields.name: owner
struct_fields.comment: The owner of the unit the brigade is in - the three-character tag here, the id at +0x98 - distinct from `builder` at +0x34. Written by AddRegimentToUnit from the unit's owner (CUnit +0x124/+0x128, 0x5BE6B5) and by CUnit_SetOwner for every brigade of a unit changing hands (0x5BC4ED); CUnit::LoadKey and its wing case copy the unit's as a brigade is read, and Deliver writes the line's country. So it is the owner, not the controller - and for a lent unit the host, its unit's owner. CDistributeUpgrade::Distribute copies it into builder at a whole level. CAirCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers resolves a country out of it for the wing's BM_RADAR_STATION technology scaling (0x16D0A6/0x16D0B0) and passes it to CWeather::AirCombatEffect for BM_WEATHER (0x16D109/0x16D100), in both cases in preference to the parent unit's owner.
struct_fields.revises: who writes it, which settles owner against controller (was 'not established')
struct_fields.evidence: Store scan for [r+0x94]/[r+0x98] pairs: 0x5BE6BB (AddRegimentToUnit: `mov edx,[edi+0x124]; mov [ebx+0x94],edx; mov eax,[edi+0x128]; mov [ebx+0x98],eax; mov [ebx+0xB0],edi`), 0x5BC4ED (CUnit_SetOwner's walk of +0x38), 0x5B73C9/0x5B7561/0x5B79C6 (CUnit::LoadKey's regiment, ship and wing cases, from [unit+0x124]), 0x484F2C (Deliver, from the line's +0x48/+0x4C). Wrong if a writer from a controller field turned up; none of the 166 pair hits reads one.

struct_fields.name: expeditionary_units_lent
struct_fields.comment: **The units this country has lent out as expeditionary forces** - its second unit list, right after units (+0xBAC). CUnit::ReturnFromExpedition unlinks a returning unit from its expeditionary_owner's list here (0x502120-0x502143); AnnexCountry walks the annexed country's (0x4E86AF) recalling each; the reinforcement share walks it after units and the upgrade share before them, each skipping units with an expeditionary owner in +0xBAC - so a lender reinforces and upgrades what it lent.
struct_fields.revises: the upgrade share walks this list first, not after +0xBAC
struct_fields.evidence: CDistributeUpgrade::Distribute reads +0xBBC at 0x51CF6D and walks it to 0x51D041 before reading +0xBAC at 0x51D04A; both loops append to the same list (tail at [esp+0x6C]) and prepend a +0xA4 unit. CDistributeReinforcement::Distribute's record has +0xBAC then +0xBBC, not re-read here.

struct_fields.name: builder
struct_fields.comment: who is building it, saved as `builder` where its id half (+0x54) is not 0. CConstructUnitCommand::Execute gives a line the command's builder, or the country where its id is 0, and CUpgradeRegimentCommand::Execute the brigade's owner - so every military line ordered in play names its country or a licence's seller; **a line out of the history files has none** (none of the 30 in Germany1936_01_01_00, all 297 in Ireland1941_07_16_07). **Read live**: the same as `country` on every military item and the no-country tag `---` on every building and convoy one
struct_fields.revises: a history file's line has none, which the live read did not see
struct_fields.evidence: Counted in the saves: `builder=` under `military_construction` 0 of 30 lines in the start save, 50 of 79 four days on (the 29 left from the history files lack it), 297 of 297 in July 1941. The two Execute records already say builder = the command's or the country, and builder = owner.

slots_noted: CDistributeUpgrade::Distribute is slot 0 of its table and already recorded there; only its comment changes
